competitors.title: real time proof of reserves is a big deal. if USD1 is publishing live supply and backing onchain thr
competitors.description:
real time proof of reserves is a big deal. if USD1 is publishing live supply and backing onchain through chainlink and bitgo, that raises the bar on transparency. after terra and the 2022 collapses, that kind of visibility matters. regulators have been clear about this too. the IMF and FSB both emphasized reserve quality, redemption rights, and ongoing disclosure in their stablecoin guidance. so on the issuer side, this is progress

1. proof of reserves only answers one question: is the stablecoin backed?

2. it doesn’t answer the other one: what happens when that stablecoin is actually used at scale?

stablecoin supply has doubled in the past two years and more volume is moving into payments, treasury, and cross border flows, not just trading. visa’s onchain dashboards show billions in settlement volume. as that grows, the exposure grows with it. public chains make balances, transfer sizes, and counterparties visible by default and it is NOT fine for running payroll, managing treasury, or executing OTC size

so transparency at the reserve level and confidentiality at the transaction level are not opposites

this is why confidential stablecoins become more important as proof of reserves improves. if the backing is verifiable in real time, the next risk is operational leakage (competitors tracking flows, bots inferring strategy, analytics firms mapping business relationships, etc)

@0xfairblock fits into that layer because it does not change the asset or weaken reserve transparency. it works with the same USDC, USDT, or even USD1 and encrypts the sensitive parts of transfers like amounts and balances, while wallets remain visible and selective disclosure stays possible for audits or compliance
